stories.title: Vornado Sells 49% Stake in 90 Park Avenue to Sixth Street, DivcoWest
stories.excerpt: Vornado Realty Trust has new partners at one of its Midtown office properties. The firm has sold a 49 percent stake in 90 Park Avenue, its 41-story Class A office building three blocks south of Grand Central Terminal, to Sixth Street and DivcoWest at a valuation of $722.5 million. Vornado announced the transaction Tuesday, not identifying the buyers, but sources later confirmed Sixth Street and DivcoWest are the lucky two. Eastdil Secured Savills’ Gary Phillips and Will Silverman repped Vornado — which will retain a majority stake in the property and also continue to lease and manage it — in the transaction, which is expected to close in December. Newmark’s Adam Spies, Josh King and Adam Doneger represented Sixth Street in the deal. Located a hop, skip and a jump from Grand Central, the 41-story, 990,000-square-foot 90 Park Avenue underwent a $70 million capital improvement program in 2016 that included a modernized lobby, destination elevators and upgraded mechanical systems. The building’s current occupancy rate is around 95 percent, sources said. In March 2025, alternative investment firm Balbec Capital signed a 13,200-square-foot lease to move its New York City office to 90 Park Avenue, while Swiss commodities trading and mining company Glencore also took 44,968 square feet at the property that month. In conjunction with the sale, a $500 million non-recourse loan is in the works, according to a release from Vornado, with the firm banking on net proceeds of $575 million after costs and loan reserves. Further info on said loan couldn’t be gleaned. Eastdil, Newmark, Sixth Street and DivcoWest declined to comment. Cathy Cunningham can be reached at ccunningham@commercialobserver.com and Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.

stories.summary: Vornado has sold a 49 percent minority stake in 90 Park Avenue, a 41-story, 990,000-square-foot Class A office tower three blocks south of Grand Central Terminal, to Sixth Street and DivcoWest at a $722.5 million valuation. The property is currently 95 percent occupied and underwent a $70 million modernization in 2016. Vornado will retain the majority stake and continue leasing and managing the building through the December closing.

Demonstrates capital flight from office to alternative assets, indirectly supporting multifamily demand in Gateway markets as office relocations may push some tenants/workers to rented apartments.

stories.title: Strada pitches apartments, for-sale townhomes facing Presidio after $52M property purchase

The property once housed St. Anne’s Home, a skilled nursing facility operated by the Little Sisters of the Poor.  Strada’s proposal calls for an eight-story, 262-unit apartment building along Lake Street and 45 for-sale townhomes on the hillside toward West Pacific Avenue and the Presidio. Strada paid $52 million for the property.  The […]This article originally appeared on The Real Deal. Click here to read the full story.

262-unit apartments (8-story) + 45 for-sale townhomes; 31 affordable units at 50% AMI; 262 parking spaces

stories.summary: Strada Investment Group filed plans for a 307-unit mixed-use development on a 6-acre site in Presidio Terrace, San Francisco, including an eight-story, 262-unit apartment building and 45 for-sale townhomes. The project includes 31 affordable units for households earning 50 percent of area median income, 262 parking spaces, and landscaped terraces. Strada paid $52 million for the former St. Anne's Home nursing facility and designed the project to meet minimum density under San Francisco's Family Zoning Plan.
stories.impact: DEMAND SIGNAL in San Francisco: Family Zoning Plan's density incentives are activating multifamily supply in underutilized sites (nursing homes, industrial). Strada's deliberate mixed-tenure approach (rentals + for-sale) signals financing flexibility—developers hedging execution risk in uncertain rate environment. This is a template for other Bay Area developers to convert non-residential assets into housing supply ahead of 2031 state mandate.

stories.title: Accounting Firm Mitchell Titus Returns to Rudin’s One Battery Park Plaza
stories.excerpt: Mitchell & Titus, LLP will relocate its New York headquarters to One Battery Park Plaza, Rudin’s 35-story office tower in Lower Manhattan. The largest minority-controlled accounting firm in the U.S., Mitchell Titus will occupy 8,289 square feet. As part of its 11-year lease, the firm, formerly a longtime tenant, is expected to return to the tower in the second quarter of 2027. “Mitchell Titus’ return to One Battery Park Plaza is a testament to quality ownership and our commitment to delivering best-in-class work environments across New York City,” said Kevin Daly, VP of office leasing at Rudin. “This agreement adds to a banner year of leasing momentum at the building, and we look forward to welcoming Mitchell Titus back.” Rudin was represented in-house by Daly and Craig Panzirer, SVP, head of office leasing. Mitchell Titus was represented by Shawna O. Menifee, principal of Savills affiliate Integrative Partners. The lease was part of a 'banner year' of leasing momentum at the property.

stories.title: Partnership With Related and BH Group Lands $38M for Waterfront Fort Lauderdale Asset
stories.excerpt: A partnership including BH Group, PEBB Enterprises and Related Group have obtained $38.4 million to refinance a mixed-use waterfront property in Fort Lauderdale where a rental tower is set to rise. Deutsche Bank provided the financing backing the Quay, a 72,904-square-foot asset between 1535 and 1515 SE 17th Street, facing the Stranahan River in Fort Lauderdale’s Harbordale neighborhood. The 7-acre property features three buildings, including a two-story office building, and a six-slip marina. “It’s a waterfront property with great visibility and a location that connects residents, convention visitors and cruise travelers,” Ian Weiner, president and CEO of PEBB Enterprises, said in a statement. “This financing gives us a strong foundation as we move toward the next chapter for the property.” In 2024, the partnership purchased the Quay for $48.5 million. It plans to build a 33-story multifamily tower on what’s now the property’s surface parking lot. A representative for the owners did not respond to a request inquiring about when construction would begin. The development — approved by city officials last year — is expected to house 5,000 square feet of commercial space and more than 750 parking spots and 521 units, 40 percent of which would be priced within 40 percent of area’s median income thanks to the Live Local Act. The Florida law provides developers tax breaks and speedy approvals in return for including workforce housing in their projects. Besides the Quay, the trio have partnered on the redevelopment of the Office Depot headquarters in Boca Raton. Earlier this month, Wells Fargo supplied a $177 million loan for the construction of a 544-unit multifamily complex on the 28-acre campus. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BH Group, PEBB Enterprises, Related Group secure $38.4M refinance via Deutsche Bank for The Quay waterfront property, Fort Lauderdale

stories.summary: A partnership of BH Group, PEBB Enterprises, and Related Group has obtained $38.4 million in refinancing from Deutsche Bank for The Quay, a 72,904-square-foot waterfront mixed-use property in Fort Lauderdale's Harbordale neighborhood. The partnership acquired the 7-acre site in 2024 for $48.5 million and plans to build a 33-story multifamily tower on the surface parking lot to deliver approximately 521 rental units.
stories.impact: CAPITAL & DEMAND SIGNAL for South Florida (Fort Lauderdale): Tier-1 developers (Related, BH, PEBB) are refinancing to fund major multifamily starts in Harbordale, a secondary waterfront location. Deutsche Bank's willingness to lend at $73.7k/unit suggests strong lender conviction on South Florida rents and absorption. Signals capital mobilization for 2025–2027 starts; watch for rent growth as these units enter market 2027–2028.

stories.title: Mason Tenders District Council Signs 10-Year Extension at 520 Eighth Ave.
stories.excerpt: GFP Real Estate announced that the Mason Tenders’ District Council Trust Funds, which provide employee benefits to active and retired workers in the construction industry, have signed a 10-year lease extension for 40,000 square feet of office space at 520 Eighth Ave. The transaction was handled in-house by Matthew Mandell, senior managing director of GFP, with no outside brokerage firm involved. “The Mason Tenders District Council Trust Funds have had a presence at 520 Eighth Ave. for more than two decades, and we’re glad the organization will be staying for another 10 years,” said Mandell. “This agreement gives them long-term certainty in a location that has worked for them, along with improvements to their existing space.” The organization, which first moved into the building in 2001, will continue using the space for its administrative offices. Located in the Penn District, 520 Eighth Ave. is among Manhattan’s most prominent nonprofit office buildings. The post Mason Tenders District Council Signs 10-Year Extension at 520 Eighth Ave. appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.title: Fernmoor Lines Up $85M Debt Financing on Two NJ Multifamily Projects
stories.excerpt: CBRE has arranged an $85-million debt financing for Mi-Place at First Radio and Mi-Place at Plainfield Station on behalf of Fernmoor, a leading multifamily developer active in New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Delaware. The financing was provided by PGIM and arranged by CBRE’s Matthew Klauer. The first asset, Mi-Place at First Radio, consists of a recently completed 218-unit apartment building in Roselle Park, NJ. The second asset, Mi-Place at Plainfield Station, is a 71-unit Plainfield, NJ development project scheduled for completion in early 2027. Both properties provide rail service to New York City via NJ Transit. “Fernmoor continues to raise the bar for suburban multifamily development,” said Klauer. “Both projects, touting superior locations and best-in-class finishes, are well-positioned for long-term success. It was a true pleasure to work with Fernmoor’s creative and motivated team.” The developer currently has four more Mi-Place projects under development. The post Fernmoor Lines Up $85M Debt Financing on Two NJ Multifamily Projects appeared first on Connect CRE.

Fernmoor's pipeline expansion (four more projects) indicates healthy underwriting and suggests continued capital availability for quality suburban multifamily in NJ/PA corridor.

stories.title: Atlantic Capital Closes Sale of Old Navy, Chase Bank in Nashua
stories.excerpt: Atlantic Capital Partners arranged the $14.475-million sale of 232 Daniel Webster Hwy., a stabilized 3.19-acre retail asset in Nashua, NH, near the Massachusetts border and 30 miles north of Boston. Justin Smith, head of capital markets, led the transaction, representing the seller and procuring the buyer, both of whom were undisclosed. The property consists of two freestanding buildings totaling 27,686 square feet: a 25,093-square-foot building leased to Old Navy and a 2,593-square-foot pad site leased to Chase Bank. Positioned four miles from downtown Nashua, the fully leased asset provides immediate cash flow in one of Southern New Hampshire’s most productive retail corridors. “Assets of this caliber in Southern New Hampshire’s primary trade area represent exceptionally rare investment opportunities,” said Smith. “The combination of creditworthy, long-term tenancy and a dominant regional retail node generated significant investor demand throughout the marketing process.” The post Atlantic Capital Closes Sale of Old Navy, Chase Bank in Nashua appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: Atlantic Capital Partners has arranged the $14.475 million sale of a 3.19-acre retail asset in Nashua, NH, near the Massachusetts border and 30 miles north of Boston. The property consists of two freestanding buildings (27,686 total square feet) leased to Old Navy and Chase Bank, providing stable, long-term cash flow in Southern New Hampshire's primary retail corridor.

stories.title: Netflix Buys Historic Radford Studio Center in L.A. for $380M
stories.excerpt: Netflix has acquired one of Los Angeles’ landmark film and television studios at a steep discount, as the region’s struggling entertainment industry continues to weigh on production real estate. The streaming giant announced Tuesday that it is purchasing the 55-acre, 1.2 million-square-foot Radford Studio Center in Studio City for $380 million from Goldman Sachs. The price is a 79 percent discount from the $1.85 billion that Hackman Capital Partners and its investors paid for the property in 2021. The acquisition follows Hackman’s default on a $1.1 billion mortgage, which led to Goldman Sachs taking control of the property. The studio received no bids at a foreclosure auction Tuesday morning, approximately an hour before Netflix announced the deal, according to Bloomberg. Netflix expects the deal to close Tuesday evening. The company plans to keep Radford operating as a working production studio, with existing productions continuing uninterrupted. Opened in 1928, Radford has hosted television classics including “Seinfeld,” “Gunsmoke,” “Gilligan’s Island” and “The Mary Tyler Moore Show.” The acquisition comes as Southern California’s production downturn continues to pressure studio owners. Hackman has faced distress across several properties, including Television City, the 25-acre Fairfax District studio where lenders led by Deutsche Bank moved toward foreclosure earlier this year. The company also faced pressure involving Manhattan Beach Studios, while Fortress Investment Group foreclosed on its Sony Animation campus in Culver City. Los Angeles-area film and television employment declined 36 percent from 2022 through 2025, according to the Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity. Production shoot days fell nearly 5 percent annually in the most recent quarter, according to FilmLA. The acquisition follows Hackman's default on a $1.1 billion mortgage. Netflix plans to maintain the facility as an operating production studio.
stories.impact: COST & CAPITAL SIGNAL for Los Angeles: Distressed asset sales in entertainment real estate underscore the secular contraction in traditional film/TV production and studio demand. This capital destruction (79% loss) has second-order implications for LA multifamily: (1) reduced demand from production workers and studios seeking office/production space means less job/wage growth in some LA submarkets; (2) conversely, underutilized studio backlots may eventually convert to housing (zoning permitting), adding supply. Near-term: reduced cost-of-living upward pressure in West LA if entertainment jobs migrate out or shrink.

stories.title: Amtrak’s U-turn throws Justin Ishbia’s South Loop stadium plan into doubt
stories.excerpt: Amtrak is spiking its plans to build a $900 million maintenance facility in Bridgeport, potentially closing off Chicago White Sox owner-in-waiting Justin Ishbia’s route to build a new ballpark for the team in his proposed Railyards development.  The plans to effectively swap out the White Sox, who play at Rate Field in Bridgeport, for a noisy maintenance facility earned the scorn of residents and local political figures alike.  The plans were abandoned after the Federal Railroad Administration said that $572 million in grant funding earmarked for the project became unsure due to previously undisclosed costs, according to Crain’s.  In August, […]This article originally appeared on The Real Deal. Click here to read the full story.
bullets: Amtrak cancels $900M Bridgeport maintenance facility; FRA calls project 'fiscally untenable,' additional $700M costs cited

stories.summary: Amtrak has canceled plans to build a $900 million maintenance facility in Bridgeport, Chicago, after the Federal Railroad Administration determined the project was 'fiscally untenable' due to previously undisclosed costs totaling an additional $700 million. The cancellation jeopardizes Justin Ishbia's proposed Railyards mixed-use development, which included a new White Sox stadium, at Amtrak's defunct 14th Street Coach Yard. Ishbia's purchase option for the team expires in 2029, coinciding with the team's lease expiration at Rate Field.
stories.impact: DEMAND & DEVELOPMENT RISK in Chicago South Loop/Bridgeport: The collapse of the Amtrak maintenance facility project removes a major site-control uncertainty but also signals dwindling capital and political will for the Railyards mixed-use development. Ishbia's option window (2029) is narrowing, and without Amtrak's relocation clearing Rate Field, the catalyst for a major mixed-use/stadium development evaporates. Expect South Loop/Bridgeport multifamily demand to remain fragmented and project-dependent rather than catalyzed by a singular sports/anchor tenant draw. Developers should view this as a 2–3 year window to acquire alternative parcels before Ishbia's option expires.

stories.title: Law Firms Expand Office Footprints as Leasing Nears Annual Record
stories.excerpt: U.S. law firms are on pace for a second straight record year of office leasing, with many still looking to expand their real estate footprints. The legal sector leased nearly 5 million square feet of office space in the third quarter of 2026, up 23 percent from the same period last year and the strongest third quarter on record, according to a report released Tuesday by Cushman & Wakefield. Law firms have collectively leased 17.5 million square feet through the first nine months of 2026, up 21 percent compared to 2025, and just 1.4 million square feet shy of the annual record set last year. “Law firm demand has not only held its pace, it has accelerated,” David C. Smith, Cushman & Wakefield’s head of Americas insights, said in a statement. “Every quarter of 2026 has outpaced its 2025 counterpart, and with one quarter remaining, the sector is positioned to surpass last year’s record total. “What stands out is that this growth is coming from firms expanding their footprints, not simply maintaining their size,” Smith added. The country’s 10 largest legal office markets accounted for 3.1 million square feet of leasing in the third quarter, and 11.2 million square feet of activity so far this year. The annual figure is just 100,000 square feet below the markets’ combined annual record set last year. New York City led all markets with 1.1 million square feet of leasing by legal firms in the third quarter. Atlanta was No. 2 with 454,000 square feet, marking its strongest quarter for legal sector leasing since 2017. Washington, D.C., accounted for 8 percent of third-quarter leasing nationwide, followed by Los Angeles at 6 percent, and Boston and San Francisco at 4 percent each. Meanwhile, Chicago and New York City have each already surpassed their 2025 law firm leasing totals. Demand also extended well beyond the country’s traditional legal hubs. Watch for law firm cluster expansions to signal talent inflows and potential wage-led rent growth in those metros.

stories.title: Hudson River Trading Expands to 551K SF at 3 World Trade Center
stories.excerpt: Hudson River Trading (HRT), a leading electronic and quantitative trading firm, has added a large chunk of office space to its global headquarters at 3 World Trade Center. HRT, which moved into its Financial District home in 2018, just signed a lease to add 340,000 square feet to its existing 211,207-square-foot office at 175 Greenwich Street, according to landlord Silverstein Properties. The new expansion brings HRT’s total footprint at 3 World Trade Center to approximately 551,207 square feet. The 15-year expansion lease had an asking rent between $110 and $150 per square foot, according to a source familiar with the deal. Before moving into 3 World Trade Center, HRT leased 70,000 square feet at 4 World Trade Center starting in 2016. Its relocation to 3 World Trade Center in 2018 gave it 136,000 square feet of office space, and HRT later added another 75,207 square feet to its footprint in 2021. The trading firm’s latest expansion deal brings the 80-story 3 World Trade Center to 98 percent occupancy, according to Silverstein. “Hudson River Trading is home to some of the most creative and brilliant people in New York, and its extraordinary growth at the World Trade Center is a testament to the appeal of this location,” Jeremy Moss, executive vice president at Silverstein, said in a statement. “Today’s announcement reflects the company’s confidence in Lower Manhattan and the advantages of working in a modern, highly connected building that can grow with its tenants.” A spokesperson for HRT added that the expansion represents “an investment in our people and in our future.” Moss represented Silverstein in-house in the deal, alongside a CBRE team of Mary Ann Tighe, Ken Meyerson, Evan Haskell and Caroline Merck. Sacha Zarba, Chris Corrinet and Jeff Fischer, also from CBRE, brokered the deal for HRT. A spokesperson for CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. stories.title: Irvine Retail Center Sells for $31.4M
stories.excerpt: Trade Marketplace, a 32,560-square-foot retail center in Irvine, sold for a reported $31.4 million ($964/sf). The property, located at 2222 and 2272 Michelson Drive, was acquired by an undisclosed private investor. Situated on just over three acres, Trade Marketplace comprises two buildings featuring a mix of traditional retail suites and an indoor-outdoor food hall. Originally built in 1989, the property was repositioned in 2017. Tenants include HiroNori Craft Ramen, Financial Partners Credit Union, Domino’s Pizza and Subway, along with a collection of independent dining and service businesses. The center is located within the Irvine Business Complex, near John Wayne Airport and Interstate 405. The surrounding one-mile radius contains approximately 18.4 million square feet of office space and 11,500 multifamily units. Christopher Smith and Andrey Mindirgasov with Colliers represented the buyer in the transaction. The seller, Dream Square Irvine LLC, an entity managed by Japan-based Daiwa House Group, acquired the property in 2019 for $30.75 million. The asset was previously marketed for sale in 2023. The post Irvine Retail Center Sells for $31.4M appeared first on Connect CRE.

The property comprises two buildings featuring traditional retail and an indoor-outdoor food hall, with tenants including HiroNori Craft Ramen, Financial Partners Credit Union, Domino's Pizza, and Subway. Located in the Irvine Business Complex near John Wayne Airport and Interstate 405, the property sits within a one-mile radius containing 18.4 million square feet of office space and 11,500 multifamily units.

Developers should view Irvine as mature, not growth-oriented.

This replicates across Fort Lauderdale's North Flagler/Harbordale strips—expect rapid multifamily starts 2025–2026, with absorption pressure 2027–2028.

stories.title: Acqualina developer Trump Group takes over Casablanca Miami Beach condo buyout

The property, recognizable by its valet entrance with statues of four men partially wrapped in white towels holding up the overhang, has been at the center of other attempted buyouts. Earlier this year, Sagar Desai’s Activate Hospitality […]This article originally appeared on The Real Deal. Click here to read the full story.
bullets: Trump Group (not affiliated with Trump Organization) acquires majority ownership of Casablanca condo-hotel buyout group, Miami Beach
10-story, 357-unit oceanfront property at 6345 Collins Avenue (built 1948); condo termination vote planned for December
Activate Hospitality remains involved; property converted from residential condos to hotel/short-term rental operation
stories.summary: The Trump Group has acquired majority ownership of the group leading the buyout of the Casablanca condo-hotel in Miami Beach at 6345 Collins Avenue, where it plans to operate the property as a hotel. The 10-story, 357-unit oceanfront property was built in 1948 and has been operated with many units as short-term rentals. A condo termination vote is scheduled for December, and Trump Group is refurbishing units as part of its takeover.
stories.impact: SUPPLY SIGNAL for Miami Beach: The Casablanca's conversion from residential condos to hotel/STR operation reduces long-term rental supply on Miami Beach's Collins Avenue oceanfront corridor. However, the broader trend of condo terminations and hotel conversions signals STR oversupply and owner consolidation. For multifamily developers, this indicates: (1) Miami Beach's condo-hotel market is normalizing post-pandemic; (2) residential rental apartments (purpose-built multifamily) may outperform condos/conversions due to operational simplicity; (3) expect continued condo-to-hotel conversions through 2027, reducing traditional rental supply but creating operational/financing risk for converted assets.

The towers are planned near West Palm’s […]This article originally appeared on The Real Deal. Click here to read the full story.
bullets: Terra and BH Group plan two 30-story condo towers on West Palm Beach waterfront (North Flagler Drive), 218 units total
1.54-acre site in contract from developer Jeff Greene; architects SOM; seeking height bonuses for ~$6M in park contributions
Market context: Currie Park redevelopment ($35.5M) opening spring 2027; North Flagler experiencing condo 'frenzy'
stories.summary: Terra and BH Group have filed plans for two 30-story condo towers on the West Palm Beach waterfront at 2085 North Flagler Drive, planning 218 condo units and 5,160 square feet of retail. The developers are under contract to purchase the 1.54-acre site from developer Jeff Greene and are seeking height bonuses in exchange for approximately $6 million in contributions to the nearby Currie Park redevelopment ($35.5 million, opening spring 2027). SOM is the architect.
stories.impact: DEMAND & SUPPLY SIGNAL for West Palm Beach North Flagler: The North Flagler waterfront corridor is experiencing a condo development boom (Terra, BH, Related/Jorge Pérez all active), signaling strong condo demand from buyers seeking walkable waterfront lifestyle ahead of Currie Park's spring 2027 opening. This is a DEMAND CATALYST—the park reopening will increase foot traffic and amenity appeal, justifying pre-sales and expedited starts. However, condo-focused development (not rentals) on this corridor suggests investor and owner-occupant demand; multifamily developers should note that North Flagler may be saturated for apartments by 2028, favoring for-sale product. Watch for condo absorption rates and pricing—if units struggle to sell, capital may pivot to rental projects in secondary West Palm locations (Northwood, Lake Worth).

Founder and CEO Adi Chugh now lives in South Florida, and in 2026, the region alone accounted for more than half of the firm’s closings of $10 billion in originations, Chugh said.  In a country awash in capital, Chugh says most […]This article originally appeared on The Real Deal. Click here to read the full story.
bullets: Tyko Capital (Paul Singer's Elliott Investment Management) sets Florida record: $817M construction loan (sole lender), funded in-house
In 2026, Tyko closed >50% of $10B in originations in South Florida; founder Adi Chugh relocated to region
Tyko focuses on 'top sponsor, top asset, top market' (rejects 95% of deals); lender emphasis on reliability vs. price
stories.summary: Tyko Capital, a New York-based private credit firm backed by Paul Singer's Elliott Investment Management, has set a Florida record by funding an $817 million construction loan entirely in-house. In 2026, South Florida accounted for more than 50 percent of Tyko's $10 billion in total originations. Founder and CEO Adi Chugh has relocated to the region and reports deploying over $2.5 billion in construction and predevelopment lending for the 12 months ending October 31, 2026. Tyko rejects 95 percent of deal submissions, focusing exclusively on 'top sponsor, top asset, top market' opportunities.
stories.impact: CAPITAL SIGNAL for South Florida (multifamily luxury/condo segment): Tyko Capital's major South Florida deployment ($2.5B+ in 12 months, $817M single loan) signals that alternative lenders (non-bank) are aggressively filling construction capital gap left by traditional bank pullback. Tyko's selectivity ('top sponsor, top asset, top market') and emphasis on execution reliability over price suggests capital is competitive but cautious—favoring established sponsors (Related, BH, Pebb, Terra) on marquee waterfront/urban locations (Miami, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach). For emerging/secondary sponsors or B+ submarkets: financing will be constrained. Expect 2025–2027 starts to concentrate among tier-1 developers in tier-1 locations; second-tier projects will face execution risk and elevated cost of capital.
